entities.summary: Vincenzo Sangermano, C.R.S.P., was an Italian Roman Catholic priest and missionary of the Barnabite Order, who traveled to South-East Asia in the late 1700s and worked in Burma from 1783 to 1806. He served in the former Ava Kingdom and Bago, Burma. After his return to Italy, he was placed in charge of the house of his Order, in Arpino. He planned to return to Burma, but died before he could set sail. He is the author of A Description of the Burmese Empire, translated into English and posthumously published in 1833, which proved a valuable source of information for the later study of Burma and its people.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sangermano's work on Burma provided valuable information for later study, influencing European understanding of the region and its people. His account is considered a primary source for understanding Burmese history and culture.
